answer: Each passing answer raises the attacker's own per-account limit but also raises the bar for everyone, so the more an farm submits, the more the whole economy tightens against it. This endures because unearned rewards carry forward into the next pool, so even when a farm fails the economy recycles the loss rather than rewarding it. This means an attacker must choose: either run a few high-quality identities, or many worthless ones — and neither option beats honest participation. Consider a inlet as the anchor of the cost. A plume stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a forge...
